title: Yara and the Signal
premise: Hazel Dravenmoor, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Perihelion, has spent twelve years hauling cargo through contested orbits between Earth and the breakaway colonies. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, he discovers the anomaly is a message encoded in spacetime itself — left by Yara, the station's long-dead original engineer, whose consciousness persists in the relay's quantum lattice. The message contains proof that Earth's government deliberately caused the colony war's first atrocity, and delivering it will either force a peace or trigger Earth's final scorched-earth transmission loop. Hazel must choose between preserving his own fragile survival and broadcasting a truth that kills him with it; in the end he sends it, dying as the lattice absorbs him beside Yara, while both fleets stand down under the weight of what they've heard.
about_author: Tamsin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for automated cargo systems before turning to fiction. They live off-grid on a decommissioned listening post, where they claim the silence improves their prose.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine cargo haul through contested orbit establishes his isolation, his failing equipment, and his bitter routine aboard the Perihelion relay station. He talks to the ship's half-broken AI out of loneliness. Emotional beat: numb endurance masking grief for a world that forgot him.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; Hazel is thrown from his bunk mid-haul and nearly lost to open space. Instruments record impossible readings — mass appearing from nothing. Emotional beat: terror giving way to a dangerous, unfamiliar thrill of wonder.

chapters.title: The Lattice Wakes
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Investigating the station's sealed lower decks, Hazel finds a quantum lattice humming with residual patterns no one has touched in decades. The AI stutters a single word it shouldn't know: 'Yara.' Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: fragments of Yara Voss, the station's dead engineer, surfacing through the lattice as sensory echoes. She remembers building the relay and hiding something inside it. Hazel realizes the flicker was her doing. Emotional beat: eerie intimacy with a ghost.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest 77
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cross-referencing old manifests, Hazel finds a shipment erased from records twelve years ago — the same week the war's first atrocity occurred. The station logged it. Someone wanted the log destroyed. Emotional beat: the slow cold of realizing he's holding something lethal.

chapters.title: The Patrol
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. An Earth patrol vessel docks unannounced, ostensibly resupplying, actually sweeping for 'anomalous emissions.' Hazel hides the lattice evidence and plays the broken hermit. Emotional beat: claustrophobic performance, every word a minefield.

chapters.title: What Yara Buried
chapters.summary: Yara's POV (lattice memory). Flashback: Yara discovered Earth's fleet deliberately triggered the colony disaster to justify the war, encoded the proof into the lattice, and died ensuring it would wait for a witness. Emotional beat: righteous fury tempered by fear she'd never be believed.

chapters.title: The Loop
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel decodes Earth's contingency protocol buried in his own maintenance codes: if the truth broadcasts, Earth triggers its last transmission loop — a scorched-earth signal that burns every relay, including him. Emotional beat: betrayal by the very system that kept him alive.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Hazel and the lattice-Yara converse directly for the first time, her voice assembled from archived logs and his own imagination filling gaps. She asks him to finish what she started. He refuses — at first. Emotional beat: reluctant companionship across death.

chapters.title: Colony Signal
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A colonial freighter, damaged and drifting, hails the station seeking refuge. Among them is a young archivist, Sef, hunting the same erased manifest. Hazel must decide whether to trust a stranger from the other side. Emotional beat: cautious hope, first human contact in years.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reveals the colonies believe Earth committed the atrocity but lack proof; their hardliners plan retaliation regardless. Hazel realizes delivering the truth could stop them — or hand zealots a weapon. Emotional beat: the burden of evidence without context.

chapters.title: The Patrol Returns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The Earth patrol comes back early, suspicious, and demands full access. Sef hides in the cargo bay while Hazel stalls with forged diagnostics. The lattice flickers dangerously close to detection. Emotional beat: white-knuckle deception, friendship forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The patrol finds traces of the lattice activity and arrests Hazel, planning to tow the station to Earth for demolition. Sef escapes into the station's guts, guided by Yara's whispers only she can hear. Emotional beat: guilt, resolve, the strange comfort of a dead woman's voice.

chapters.title: Inside the Machine
chapters.summary: Sef's POV navigating the station's depths; interwoven with Hazel interrogated aboard the patrol ship, buying time with bureaucratic stonewalling. Yara's memories grow clearer to Sef — the lattice is reaching for a second mind. Emotional beat: transformation, unwilling initiation.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Offered amnesty in exchange for confirming the lattice is malfunctioning junk, Hazel confronts twelve years of complicity through silence. He signs nothing. Emotional beat: the quiet dignity of finally choosing a side.

chapters.title: Broadcast Window
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reaches the transmitter core and learns the broadcast requires a living mind to anchor the quantum signature — Yara's design demands a witness who understands what they're sending. Both fleets' fleets converge on the station. Emotional beat: terrible clarity about the cost.

chapters.title: Fleetfall
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Earth and colonial warships take position around the Perihelion, each believing the other is about to strike. Hazel, released amid the chaos, fights his way back aboard. Emotional beat: the war arriving at his doorstep after leaving him alone for so long.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Reunited with Sef, Hazel learns the broadcast will consume whoever anchors it. Yara offers herself again — a degraded copy, enough for maybe minutes. Hazel refuses to let her burn twice. Emotional beat: love, in whatever form it takes, refusing arithmetic.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds Again
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. As the fleets power weapons, the lattice initiates the broadcast; gravity flickers once more, freezing targeting systems for nine seconds — Yara's final gift. Hazel steps into the anchor cradle. Emotional beat: calm acceptance, the opposite of the opening chapter's numbness.

chapters.title: Everything, Everywhere, At Once
chapters.summary: Hazel's dissolving POV. The truth floods every receiver in the system: manifests, recordings, Yara's testimony, Hazel's own twelve years of logs. Weapons lock, then waver, then release. The transmission loop arms — and fails, because Hazel already gave the loop everything it needed. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Ceasefire negotiations begin aboard the battered station. Sef archives Yara and Hazel's merged pattern in the lattice, now stable, now singing quietly through the relays. Ships pass the station and report hearing two voices harmonizing. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sef's POV, one year later. The war has ended; the Perihelion is a memorial and a listening post. Sef, its new keeper, receives a faint structured pulse from deep space — Yara's encoding, echoed back from somewhere impossibly far. Someone, or something, heard. Emotional beat: inheritance fulfilled; memory outliving its makers.
